solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disney film lad brought back for children

parts.note: Bambi is the 1942 Disney animation about a young deer

indicators.note: brought back says the word for the lad is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a son

explanation.surface: A Disney cartoon about a young boy being brought back for the children to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' is the reversal signal, not a cinema re-release.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambinos is Italian-derived informal English for babies or young kids.

clue.text: Foreign goalie neatly saves

indicators.note: a goalkeeper saves, but here the phrase holds or keeps the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: An overseas goalkeeper tidily stops shots on goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saves' keeps the letters inside goaLIE Neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means belonging to another country, i.e. strange or not native.

clue.text: Flattering European in the end on phone

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the preceding pieces

parts.note: a butt is the thick end of something, as of a rifle or cigarette
to ring up is to phone someone

explanation.surface: A European sweet-talking somebody at the end of a telephone call.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply follow one another: BUTT, then E, then RING UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttering up is the idiom for flattering someone to win their favour.

clue.text: General staff about to support an uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry the later pieces sit beneath the first, holding it up
in a down clue uprising means the little word is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
a staff is a pole
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A military general's staff officers backing a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reads upward in a down entry; 'to support' means the following pieces sit beneath, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the famous French military commander, an example of a general.

clue.text: Circuitous flight from Alsace airstrip's rerouted

indicators.note: rerouted suggests sending along a different path, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An aircraft's roundabout journey from a French region's runway after a change of plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rerouted' rearranges ALSACE AIRSTRIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral staircase is a winding set of steps, and a flight is a run of stairs.

clue.text: Desire to replace contents of sweet bag

indicators.note: replacing the contents means the inside letters of the next word are swapped out for the first piece

parts.note: taken as written
to ache for something is to desire it

explanation.surface: A craving for the contents of a bag of sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace contents of' swaps WEE, the middle of SWEET, for ACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed pouch, a type of little packet.

clue.text: Sailors viewed netting in the morning

indicators.note: netting means catching, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: viewed means seen
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Sailors were spotted fishing with nets early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen are mariners, people who work at sea.

clue.text: What hacker does is not totally clever

indicators.note: not totally means the word is left incomplete, its last letter dropped

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd, as in a cute move

explanation.surface: A computer hacker's work isn't entirely smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally' drops the final E of CUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacker in the old sense chops roughly with a blade, which is to slice or chop.

clue.text: Make sexy twitch in naughty soiree

indicators.note: in places the twitch within the scrambled party letters
naughty suggests misbehaving, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Adding a suggestive wink at a racy evening party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitch' is a noun here, not the verb it looks like; 'naughty' and 'in' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To eroticise something is to give it an erotic, sexual character.

clue.text: Overturned bedpan by bed? Fantastic!

indicators.note: overturned means the combined pieces are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a pot, a chamber pot, serves as a bedpan
pit is slang for bed

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled when a bedpan beside a bed is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' reverses POTPIT. PIT is British slang for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an exclamation or adjective meaning excellent, first-rate.

clue.text: Sluggishness of one caught invading country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: invading means getting into the country, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a nation is a country
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A slow invasion in which one person is captured entering a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invading' puts C inside NATION, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaction is a lack of activity, the idleness of doing nothing.

clue.text: Old French town from which Italy's withdrawn in the past

indicators.note: from which introduces the word that will lose a letter
withdrawn means pulled out, so this letter is removed

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An old town in France that Italy gave up long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice was indeed Italian until 1860, which gives the surface its history; 'from which' and 'withdrawn' together signal the removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time.

clue.text: Command revolutionary soldiers aboard metal boat

indicators.note: aboard means on the vessel, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: lead is a metal
a ship is a boat

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Mutinous troops seize control of an iron-hulled vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers are the Royal Engineers, a British army corps; 'revolutionary' and 'aboard' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is control or direction of a group.

clue.text: Player's nerves level following remedy

parts.note: a stage is a level, as in a stage of a game
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to right a wrong is to remedy it

explanation.surface: A sports player's anxiety calmed by a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' means an actor, not a sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage fright is the anxiety a performer feels before an audience.

clue.text: Fruit rot treated with aspic

indicators.note: treated suggests processed or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Decaying fruit preserved in savoury jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges ROT and ASPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Apricots are small orange stone fruits.

clue.text: Office worker's vigour after taking in new attendant

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: pep is energy or vigour
an usher is an attendant who shows people to seats

explanation.surface: A clerk regains energy once a fresh assistant is hired.
explanation.walkthrough: The online text read 'after a king in', which does not parse; printed copies had 'taking in'. 'taking in' puts N inside PEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen-pusher is a disparaging term for a clerk doing routine desk work.

clue.text: Keen songstress gets rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female singer

explanation.surface: An eager singer is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets rejected' turns DIVA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: Fabric layer poorly installed in church

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside, so these pieces go within another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hen is a layer of eggs
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A cloth covering, badly fitted in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' is the egg-producer, not a sheet of material.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a soft tufted yarn or cloth.

clue.text: Antelope switching sides to get comfy

indicators.note: switching sides means the letters at each end change places

parts.note: gnus are wildebeest, a kind of antelope

explanation.surface: A wildebeest changes position to get comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching sides' swaps the outer letters of GNUS, so G and S trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means cosy and comfortable.

clue.text: A Greek character always successful type

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A Greek who always succeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An achiever is someone who reaches goals, a successful person.

clue.text: Converts area before erecting stone home

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the rest
erecting means raising upright, so in a down entry the letters read upward

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
pad is slang for one's home

explanation.surface: Someone transforms land before building a stone house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erecting' turns STPAD into DAPTS, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to modify or transform it for a new use.

clue.text: Worked out grill attached to sides of extended household appliance

parts.note: to grill someone is to question them, to pump them for information

indicators.note: sides of means the outer letters of the next word

parts.note: an iron is a household appliance for pressing clothes

explanation.surface: Cooking on a grill attached to a big kitchen appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grill' is interrogation, not cooking. 'sides of' takes E and D from 'extended'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumped iron means lifted weights, i.e. exercised in a gym.

clue.text: Go wild striking north from hills?

indicators.note: striking means crossing out, so this letter is removed
from names the word losing the letter

parts.note: a range is a line of hills or mountains

explanation.surface: Someone going berserk on a walk through the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' and 'from' remove N from RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage is to be violently angry, to rampage.

clue.text: Cultivated king wearing robe

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so one piece is inside the garment

parts.note: a gown is a robe
R, for rex, abbreviates king

explanation.surface: A refined monarch dressed in a robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts R inside GOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown means raised or produced by cultivation, as with crops.

clue.text: Elegant parrot eating soft legume

parts.note: chic means elegant and stylish

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: the kea is a New Zealand parrot
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A smart parrot pecking at a tender bean.
explanation.definitionFit: The chickpea is a pulse, a pod-bearing plant's seed.

clue.text: Queen perhaps beginning to address court guards

indicators.note: guards means surrounds, so one piece goes inside the other
beginning to means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A queen starting to make a speech in a palace protected by guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives A, which 'guards' puts inside CT.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female domestic feline, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Learner in the past playing pool

parts.note: L is for learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars
ago means in the past
on means playing, as an actor or a game

explanation.surface: A trainee once swam in a pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' is the definition, not where the learner plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a shallow body of water cut off from the sea.

clue.text: Free traitor imprisoned by US soldiers

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is a betrayer

explanation.surface: A turncoat released from American military custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means without charge, i.e. at no cost.

clue.text: Using river, vessel entering outskirts of Reading

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other
outskirts means the edges, the first and last letters

parts.note: a tin is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A boat on the river heading into the edge of the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town west of London; 'outskirts of' and 'entering' are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Exerting means applying or employing force or influence.
